problem: Zero-shot VLM navigators (e.g. VLMnav, PIVOT) decide from discrete observations and keep history as a flat, unstructured log. This gives no spatiotemporal continuity, weak long-range planning, poor task understanding, and failures such as spinning in place.
motivation: Household robots must navigate unseen environments without prior maps or scene-specific training. The bottleneck for VLMs in long-range navigation is memory structure and task comprehension. The paper draws on the cognitive 'decentralized ontology' idea and the ventral (what) / dorsal (where) split in the brain.
key_idea: Split zero-shot end-to-end VLM navigation into a Dorsal Stream (topological map plus hierarchical semantic-spatial memory with retrieval) and a Ventral Stream (CoDe-VLM compiles the task into a knowledge graph, Exec-VLM reasons over it), backed by stuck detection and escape (Nav-Ensurance).
insight: Ablations show every component adds value: removing both streams gives SR 51.6 / SPL 18.3 on HM3Dv2, versus roughly 61 SR with the full model. Removing the Dorsal Stream alone gives 59.0 SR, and removing Nav-Ensurance mainly worsens AORI. Structured memory and task decomposition improve a generic VLM prompt-based agent, and the framework stays reasonably effective with smaller VLMs (Qwen-7B 49.5 SR).
method: Action Proposer: as in VLMnav, it generates depth-checked polar action candidates (angle, distance) within the FOV, filters them by exploration history, adds a turn-around recovery, and projects them as numbered arrows onto the image.

Topological Map: nodes store pose, image, language description, target likelihood and CLIP embedding. A node is added when a step interval S_update=3 or a distance threshold δ_sample is exceeded, and each new node is linked to its predecessor.

Hierarchical Semantic-Spatial Fusion: a 4-level memory (observation L3, area L2, room L1, environment L0) is built bottom-up by linkage clustering on combined spatial and CLIP distance. Top-down beam-search retrieval (B=5, top-K) scores nodes with 0.45 semantic + 0.30 spatial + 0.20 keyword + 0.05 recency.
CoDe-VLM: compiles the instruction or object category into a task-specific knowledge graph (description, appearance, location priors) used to verify objects and provide planning priors.

Exec-VLM: a Gemini-1.5-Pro chain-of-thought (state analysis, memory integration, goal analysis, scene assessment, path planning, action decision) picks the action from the annotated image, retrieved memory and KG.

Nav-Ensurance: stuck detection from progress efficiency η and rotation/translation ratio ρ over a sliding window; context-aware escapes (large turn in corners, back step plus random turn in narrow passages, perpendicular move when ambiguous); precision mode scales step distance by γ=0.1 near the target.
AORI metric: Area Overlap Redundancy Index measuring revisited-area ratio and normalized density (lower is better) to quantify exploration redundancy.

setting.backbone: Gemini-1.5-Pro (frozen) as main VLM; CLIP ViT-B/32 for embeddings
setting.action_space: continuous polar (r in 0.5-1.7 m, θ from 60 bins over 360°) plus stop; converted to about 9-10 discrete steps (0.25 m / 30°) per action for comparison with non-E2E methods
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, MP3D, GOAT on HM3Dv2)

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3Dv1 in Table 2 (non-E2E comparison); the ablation table used 100 episodes
numbers.extra: end-to-end steps normalized to a 500 discrete-step budget (about 60 E2E steps)

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3Dv2 in Table 2; the main Table 1a reports SR 62.0 / SPL 23.0 / AORI 50.1 on the ObjectNav benchmark (HM3Dv2)

numbers_note: Ablation tables use 100 episodes and are not listed. The ablation default on HM3Dv2 reads SR 61.0 / SPL 23.7, which differs from the 62.0 / 23.0 in Table 1a. Split names are given only as 'val'. It is unclear whether the main tables use the full split.
results: DORAEMON reaches SR 62.0 / SPL 23.0 on HM3Dv2 in the end-to-end comparison, beating VLMnav (51.6 / 18.3), and SR 24.3 / SPL 10.3 on GOAT versus VLMnav 22.1 / 9.3. Against non-E2E methods it gets the highest SR on HM3Dv2 (66.5) and MP3D (41.1), but its SPL is lower than VLFM, SG-Nav and others.
limitations: SPL is well below the best non-end-to-end methods (e.g. VLFM 32.5 on HM3Dv2), and SR on HM3Dv1 is below SGM (60.2).
It depends on a proprietary VLM (Gemini-1.5-Pro) with many hand-tuned hyperparameters. Smaller VLMs perform notably worse (Qwen-7B 49.5 SR), and ablations use only 100 episodes.
Real-world validation is only a qualitative demo in one office, and the AORI metric is newly proposed by the authors.
